slot.brief: Ionic vs covalent/metallic hydrides: identify properties like thermal stability trend down a group or electrical conductivity

stem: Which electrical behaviour is expected for calcium hydride in its solid and molten states?
options: Conducts in the solid state but not when molten
Does not conduct in the solid state but conducts when molten
Does not conduct in either state

verdicts.working: Calcium hydride is ionic: its ions are fixed in the solid but mobile when molten, so it conducts only when molten.

working:
In solid $�text{CaH}_2$, ions are fixed in the lattice, so it does not conduct.
When molten, its ions are mobile, so it conducts electricity.

Independent check: Calcium hydride is ionic: its ions are fixed in the solid but mobile when molten, so it conducts only when molten.
solution: Solid $\text{CaH}_2$ has ions fixed in the lattice, so it does not conduct electricity. When molten, its ions are mobile and carry charge, so it conducts.
